title: Dayanidhi Maran flags concerns about proposed Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Rules, 2026; urges Centre for a review
content: Mr. Maran in his letter, urging the Centre to withdraw the proposed draft rules in their current form and undertake a comprehensive review in consultation with independent animal welfare experts, scientists, veterinarians, research institutions and civil society organisations

title: How is Kerala planning to prevent child deaths linked to malnutrition and neglect? Explained
content: A State-wide vulnerability mapping will be held to identity children living in vulnerable conditions that pose a risk to their health, education, and safety. Once the vulnerable children are identified and their details collected, regular follow-ups will be held

title: Kolkata stampede: Death in the time of Durga Puja
content: On October 17, a stampede broke out at a Durga Puja pandal in north Kolkata, claiming 19 lives. The pandal, erected in a narrow space with dim lighting, was filled with people soon after it started raining. Shrabana Chatterjee and Shiv Sahay Singh report on the lapses that led to the tragedy and the questions it has raised about accountability in West Bengal, where the new government’s first Durga Puja celebrations have been marred by controversy

title: Karnataka’s coffee country: Inside its most immersive plantation stays
content: Across Coorg and Chikmagalur, estates are turning the journey from coffee cherry to cup into a reason to travel, with experiences shaped by local history, biodiversity and generations of growing knowledge

title: Karnataka SIR: Teaching on the back burner
content: Children in government and aided schools across Karnataka have not seen several of their teachers for months, for most of them have been assigned as Booth Level Officers for the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Students tell Rishita Khanna that what initially seemed like fun with many free hours, is now making them anxious...

title: Odisha moves Supreme Court against Andhra Pradesh over rural poll notice in Kotia area
content: While all the 28 villages under Kotia Gram Panchayat remain in Odisha territory, Andhra Pradesh has been claiming its rights over 21 villages. Odisha challenged this in the Supreme Court in 1968 and the court asked both States to maintain the status quo in 2006

title: Students, farmers, civil society groups continue to protest against SIR, CEC
content: Hundreds take to the streets as Yogendra Yadav, Annie Raja, and farmers’ groups join protest; police say 20 detained, one FIR resgistered

title: IndiGo extends cancellation of Saudi flights as regional tensions escalate: Indian mission
content: IndiGo has extended the cancellation of its flights to and from Saudi Arabia as regional security concerns escalate, with Riyadh routes halted until October 31, 2026 and Jeddah, Dammam, and Madinah routes until October 27, 2026, the Indian Embassy in Riyadh said.

title: Election Commission sought explanation from officials as goof-up in voter list went viral
content: “There is a possibility of mistakes when doing any work for the first time. Out of 14,81,310 entries in the voter list, there are a total of 158 entries in which the names of the voters or their relatives appear strange. The strangeness of these names is due to such a mistake,” says statement released by Chief Electoral Officer, Uttar Pradesh

title: Students protest against SIR at Mumbai University, demand arrest of CEC Gyanesh Kumar
content: Organised by the Disha Students’ Organisation and Bhagat Singh Jan Adhikar Yatra (BSJAY), the demonstration also called for the repeal of the 2023 law governing the appointment of Election Commissioners

title: Assam government to present 1st Bhupen Hazarika National Award to Usha Mangeshkar: Himanta
content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will present the award at the concluding ceremony of the singer's year-long birth centenary celebrations at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on November 29, says CM Sarma

title: Legal action ordered against officials over irregularities in voter list in Pilibhit
content: Legal action will be taken against both the current and former election officials responsible for the discrepancies found in the voter list for constituency 127 – Pilibhit, reads an official statement by the State election commission

title: Alleged confrontations between goons, cops raise law and order questions in Ernakulam
content: Senior officials in the district claim that the reported incidents are isolated cases, and that strict action is being taken against miscreants

title: No local body polls in Amaravati capital region villages of Andhra Pradesh
content: Elections in villages where land pooling is under way have been kept pending for the time being as the government is working on a separate governance framework for the mega capital city

title: Cyclonic storm likely to hit North Andhra Pradesh coast on October 28, says IMD
content: Red warnings for extremely heavy rain issued for October 27 and 28; fishermen who have ventured into the sea asked to return to shore

title: M.P. receives investment proposals of over ₹15,400 crore at semiconductor summit
content: Chief Minister Mohan Yadav said that the government also received proposals worth around ₹5,800 that have potential to generate around 10,000 employment opportunities

title: Bomb threat emails to Mumbai Mayor’s office, three Navi Mumbai schools trigger security alert
content: Prompted by the threat, law enforcement authorities have launched a comprehensive investigation to verify the authenticity of the message

title: Pregnant minor gang-raped in Rajasthan; newborn dies after delivery in deserted area
content: Afterwards, she reached a hospital, where the newborn was declared dead, prompting the hospital administration to notify local police

title: Financial insecurity drives older people to seek jobs, survey in Bengaluru finds
content: Nearly half of senior jobseekers reporting employment barriers say employers prefer younger candidates

title: MPSC paper ‘leak’: Fourth Commission official arrested, total arrests rise to 13
content: The accused, identified as Rohit Kolatakke, an assistant section officer with the MPSC, allegedly obtained the confidential question set from Abhijit Lendve, an under-secretary with the commission, who was arrested earlier in the case

title: Karnataka braces for 21,000 MW power demand in summer next year
content: According to Energy Department data, Karnataka’s power demand peaked at 18,650 MW during the summer of 2025. It subsequently touched 20,000 MW in September 2026.

title: Agriculture pumpset power load increases by 25-50%, other categories by 18% amidst rain deficit in Karnataka
content: According to sources in the Energy Department, Karnataka’s average daily electricity consumption rose to 349-362 Million Units (MU) in the first two weeks of October 2026, surpassing the record of 340 MU recorded in September.

title: India denies rejecting Iran’s request to transport medicines
content: Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “We remain in contact with our Iranian counterparts to facilitate the transport of life-saving medicines as a humanitarian gesture.”

title: Kerala artist Tom Vattakuzhy’s shows in London and Paris reflect the frailty of the human condition
content: Artist Tom Vattakuzhy on showing his works in strife-torn Paris, the excitement of Frieze Week in London and how he views his practice post the controversy surrounding his work at the Kochi Muziris Biennale

title: ‘Gem Granites’ Veeramani’s daughter detained from aircraft by SIT
content: Investigators took custody of Archana Veeramani after she boarded a flight at Chennai International Airport

title: Proposed driving licence rules raise the bar for learner’s test
content: As per draft amendments, applicants should secure 75% to pass preliminary test; licence-seekers will have to disclose more health information; there will be no fee to change licensee’s name, address

title: Punjab House passes resolution against electoral irregularities
content: Taking part in the discussion on the resolution on Day 2 of the Assembly session, Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann blamed the BJP for alleged vote ‘loot’, terming it dangerous for democracy, and demanded the scrapping of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls

title: Keralam government prioritising infrastructure development in fisheries sector, says Minister
content: Inaugurating development works completed at Puthiyappa and Koyilandy fishing harbours, Fisheries Minister V.E. Abdul Gafoor says govt. will continue to implement schemes aimed at improving the living standards of fishers

title: Keralam to conduct Statewide child vulnerability mapping
content: Meeting decides that Women and Child Development Officers in districts will be fully responsible for ensuring children’s safety and rehabilitation.

title: Congress high command asks Karnataka CM to start probe into alleged sting operation attempt
content: The Chief Minister, in an interview with a Kannada television channel, had claimed that a businessman wearing Meta AI glasses recently met him in, what he suspected, was an attempted “sting operation.”

title: Jaishankar meets Azerbaijan President, Foreign Minister as India attempts reset of ties
content: Bilateral ties had soured with Azerbaijan’s condemnation of Operation Sindoor and calls for ‘resolution’ of the Kashmir issue;  but on Friday, Azerbaijani Foreign Minister Bayramov highlighted trade, tourism, and energy ties after a ‘fruitful discussion’ with his Indian counterpart

title: Telangana CM asks officials to be prepared to convince Maharashtra for 152 m FRL barrage at Tummidihatti
content: Revanth Reddy directs them to make arrangements to draw 0.6 tmc ft additional water from Srisailam for Dindi, Achampet projects by using PRLIS pumping system

title: Bharat Petroleum’s net profit dips amid volatile crude prices in Q2
content: Bharat Petroleum’s revenues spurred 29% whilst net profit declined 22.5% on a year-over-year basis in Q2

title: PLA’s patrolling behaviour keeps LAC disturbed, Govt. says
content: MEA says “Chinese forces diverge from established patrolling patterns”; video of ITBP chief’s remarks on situation in Arunachal Pradesh removed after The Hindu’s report on the border situation; Congress slams government for suppressing information

title: Protests against SIR updates: CJP leaders vow to continue SIR protest, say Gyanesh Kumar will have to resign
content: Police detained protesters during march to ECI HQ; Samyukt Kisan Morcha and ‘People Against SIR’ platform are protesting nationwide; various trade unions and civil society organisations have pledged support to the farmers’ march

title: Delhi High Court rejects Neha Bora's plea against police notice to sign peace bond
content: HC judge, however, says that he has passed certain directions to the special executive magistrate (SEM) on providing all material to the student leader in the proceedings

title: El Nino-induced water and power crisis likely to persist until July: Revanth
content: CM asks people to save water and power; special employment guarantee scheme after Sankranti, says people should adapt to the situation as they did during the pandemic

title: Navy to host Indo-Pacific Regional Dialogue in New Delhi from November 3
content: The 3-day event will bring together policymakers and experts from 18 countries seeking to identify practical measures to strengthen regional cooperation in maritime research, ocean governance, climate resilience and emerging technologies

title: Over 100 detained as SIR protests continue in Delhi
content: Hundreds of protesters including students and farmers gathered in Delhi to demand the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. They criticized the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls for resulting in unfair voter deletions. Many demonstrators were detained by police as tensions escalated during the protest. Demonstrations have been organized in 88 cities across 18 states involving numerous organizations.

title: US detains Bishnoi rival Himanshu Bhau after 4-yr manhunt, India may get custody soon
content: Himanshu Bhau, a notorious gangster from north India, was recently captured by the FBI in Las Vegas. He has been wanted for a series of violent offenses, including multiple murders and extortion schemes that have plagued Delhi and Haryana. After escaping juvenile detention in 2020, he maintained his criminal operations through illegal networks.

title: 15-year-old girl sexually assaulted in Telangana; 7 arrested
content: Seven individuals, including three minors, were arrested in Siddipet district for allegedly assaulting a 15-year-old girl. The incident occurred on Dasara when the victim's parents were away for agricultural work. The accused reportedly took the girl to a neighboring village and returned her the following morning. The victim identified the perpetrators, leading her father to file a police complaint.

title: Five ducks, 113 all out! India A batters suffer horror show against New Zealand A
content: On a grass-covered pitch offering assistance to the fast bowlers, the Dhruv Jurel-led side had no answers to New Zealand A's disciplined attack. Five Indian batters failed to score a single run, while the top order once again failed to justify its reputation.

title: Engineer sues Nscale ahead of NYSE listing over wrongful termination claim
content: Nscale is facing a lawsuit in Norway filed by a former engineer regarding alleged wrongful dismissal and illegal practices. The engineer claims he was unfairly terminated after raising concerns related to employment conditions at Nscale’s facility. Under Norwegian law, companies must provide full rights to subcontracted personnel treated as direct employees. Nscale's operations have encountered various challenges including equipment malfunctions and contract complications.

title: 'Another little Epic Fury': Trump warns as Iran says 'don't play with fire'
content: US President Donald Trump threatened Iran with potential military action if no diplomatic agreement is reached soon. He referenced the previous operation named 'Epic Fury' while addressing supporters in Florida. Additionally, US intelligence reports indicate Iran's increased efforts to target American diplomats in the Middle East. Amidst rising tensions, the US has ordered non-emergency personnel to leave Saudi Arabia due to security concerns.

title: Selena Gomez’s charity benefit raises $2.7m for mental health
content: Selena Gomez proudly hosted the fourth annual Rare Impact Fund Benefit in Los Angeles, successfully raising significant funds for mental health initiatives. The evening took an exciting turn when her husband, Benny Blanco, bid an impressive $25,000 for a special modeling experience with Gomez’s glam team. During the event, she reaffirmed her dedication to youth mental health and introduced the Katherine Short Legacy Award, with a remarkable total of $2.

title: Haryana power cut: Homes in dark for hours, residents block roads
content: A two-day power strike in Haryana caused significant disruptions across Gurgaon and surrounding areas. Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini assured employees that no private power distribution licenses would be permitted. Outages led to water supply disruptions and industrial production halts, impacting many residents and businesses. Appeals were made by industry bodies for urgent government intervention to restore power.

title: Jason Momoa buys Sam Neill's former 4.92-hectare NZ estate for NZ$15m
content: Jason Momoa has recently acquired a significant property in Queenstown, New Zealand for NZ$15 million. The estate, formerly owned by Sir Sam Neill, demonstrates the increasing interest in the local real estate market. Property values in the region have risen significantly, attracting overseas buyers. Momoa has deep connections to New Zealand, having visited frequently for leisure and work. He has also invested in the local film industry and nightlife scene.

title: Ontario farmer turned down C$16m for 164 acres; 29 acres protected for 999 years
content: Charles Stevens and his family have decided to protect Wilmot Orchards by placing a conservation easement on the property. This easement effectively restricts future development for nearly 1,000 years, ensuring continued agricultural use. Their decision counters pressures from developers seeking to convert farmland into housing. The Stevens family aims to preserve the land for future generations of farmers.

title: 'Haven't seen this in a long time': Microsoft CEO on massive PHP flaw patch rush
content: Global corporations and government agencies are currently dealing with significant vulnerabilities discovered in PHP programming language. The vulnerabilities have led to millions of automated exploitation attempts shortly after the public disclosure. Leading technology executives, including Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, have expressed concern regarding software security. In response, emergency patches were released, urging users to update immediately. As a result, many organizations temporarily suspended online operations, prioritizing security measures.

title: Assam's Jintimani Kalita wanted only bat as child, makes India ODI debut
content: Jintimani Kalita officially kicked off her One Day International career for India against Zimbabwe on October 23, becoming the second female cricketer from Assam to don the national colors. Her cricketing path began with training among boys and utilizing borrowed gear. Previously, she was signed by the Mumbai Indians in the Women's Premier League, which opened new doors for her.

title: Nihal Sarin, Koneru Humpy clinch individual gold medals at European Chess Club Cup
content: Indian grandmasters impressed at the European Chess Club Cup 2026 in Montenegro, with Nihal Sarin winning individual gold and Pentala Harikrishna taking silver. Karthikeyan Murali secured bronze, while Arjun Erigaisi finished fourth. In the women’s event, Koneru Humpy won individual gold and helped Cercle d’Echecs de Monte-Carlo clinch the team title.

title: 'PLA strong rival': MEA says China's patrolling deviations disturb border
content: The ministry of external affairs (MEA) on Friday did not go into the specifics of the latest face-off, choosing to refer the issue to the defence ministry, but said Chinese divergence from established patrolling patterns created disturbances at the border from time to time. The official said both sides continued to use existing diplomatic and military mechanisms to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC.

title: Diljit Dosanjh's Delhi gig gets police nod amid fresh threats
content: With security concerns arising, the Delhi Police initially refused to grant permission for Diljit Dosanjh's upcoming concert. Following constructive discussions with the organisers, improved safety protocols were established, including the addition of 1,500 personnel for crowd management. Attendees will be updated about transportation options in collaboration with cab providers. The concert is officially rescheduled for October 30 at Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium.

title: Tiger Shroff targeted for praising Salman Khan in 2022, shooter tells police
content: Tiger Shroff allegedly became a target of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang after praising Salman Khan publicly. During an event for 'Heropanti 2', Shroff referred to Khan as the industry's one true tiger. An arrested shooter claimed that the gang wanted revenge for Shroff's comments at the film promotion. Police are investigating the motives behind the threats aimed at Shroff and other Bollywood personalities.

title: Amid stir, Delhi's Jamia builds wall in front of gate; university denies connection
content: Jamia Millia Islamia is constructing a wall near Gate No. 10 amid student protests currently taking place. Students have alleged that this construction is meant to limit access to their protest site on campus. Protesters are demanding student union elections and the reversal of disciplinary actions against participating students. University officials have stated that the wall construction is part of a routine security upgrade.

title: Watch: Giant waves crash into Taiwan as Typhoon Champi leaves over 500 injured; 1 dead
content: Typhoon Champi made landfall in Taiwan, resulting in one casualty and more than 500 injuries reported. The storm brought heavy rain and strong winds, leading to widespread power outages affecting over 167,000 homes. Over 240 flights were canceled due to severe weather conditions impacting transport services. Schools and offices were closed for an extended period as a precautionary measure against the storm.

title: Israel launches ‘limited counterterrorism’ op after 2 IDF troops killed in West Bank
content: In a post on X, the IDF said, "In response to the shooting attack in which 2 IDF soldiers fell, and several others were wounded, the IDF along with other security forces launched a targeted & limited counterterrorism operation in the Hebron area, from which the terrorists had emerged." The military said residents in areas where its forces are operating would be allowed to leave through three designated exit points.

title: India highlights nuclear advances, development partnerships at UNGA session
content: India has expressed its dedication to peaceful nuclear technology and support for the International Atomic Energy Agency. Several countries have acknowledged India's development assistance during the Ninth Annual India-UN Development Partnership Fund event. Ambassadors from various nations highlighted how India's support aligns with their national priorities and fosters South-South cooperation. IAEA's director-general projected significant growth in global nuclear power usage driven by technological demands.

title: Upper layer NBFCs have to list: RBI guv on Tatas; dispels doubts on Sept order
content: RBI governor Sanjay Malhotra’s comments also suggest Tata Sons is in breach of RBI rules. The consequences of continued noncompliance remain unclear. The governor declined to be drawn into the question of Noel Tata’s proposal to merge two Tata Sons subsidiaries with the holding company, a move that could help it sidestep a stock market listing.

title: 'We have to think about posting 350 first': Rauf on need for bigger totals
content: Haris Rauf said his role alongside Shaheen Afridi and Naseem Shah is to take wickets and strengthen Pakistan’s bowling attack. He stressed teamwork, middle-over breakthroughs and the need for bigger totals as ODI cricket becomes more aggressive. Rauf is also focusing on improving his pace and fitness, while backing Saim Ayub and Fakhar Zaman to contribute runs in upcoming matches.

title: Dan vs Daniel: Trump admin sues to block Alaska result if GOP candidate loses race
content: The lawsuit, filed in federal court in Alaska on Thursday, argues that the state must protect the integrity of federal elections. It asks the court to block the certification of a Peltola victory if Daniel Sullivan, a candidate from the small fishing community of Petersburg, remains on the ballot. “The United States accordingly brings this lawsuit to protect the integrity of the 2026 Senate election in Alaska,” the lawsuit says.

title: Tom Brady helped provide 750,000 meals to families in need in Tampa Bay
content: Tom Brady and Gisele Bündchen donated funds to provide 750,000 meals through Feeding Tampa Bay, supporting children, families and senior citizens in need. The contribution came shortly after the couple moved to Florida, where Brady began his career with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after 20 seasons with the New England Patriots. Their donation helped address food insecurity and supported local families facing financial hardship, highlighting their commitment to their new community.

title: Giannis Antetokounmpo reportedly invested $70 million in real estate
content: Since October 2025, NBA superstar Giannis Antetokounmpo has strategically invested approximately $70 million in various real estate ventures. His family's company, Ante, has facilitated several significant purchases, including apartment complexes in Wisconsin, Brooklyn, and Chicago. Notably, he recently acquired a lavish $13.5 million mansion in Pinecrest, Florida, after joining the Miami Heat. These investments reflect Antetokounmpo's commitment to expanding his financial portfolio beyond basketball income.

title: Video: Gunmen storm Jordan church during funeral, killing 7 and wounding 40
content: Jordan's government described the attackers as unknown assailants and said investigations were moving ahead at full speed. It did not immediately confirm whether any suspects had been arrested or killed. Footage aired by Jordanian state television showed two men appearing to carry pistols approaching the church and firing shots. A third man, apparently carrying a semi-automatic rifle, then approached and opened fire before all three ran towards the building.

title: IND vs NZ 2nd T20I: Will Ishan Kishan's injury be Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's gain?
content: Ishan Kishan has been ruled out of the second T20I match against New Zealand due to a strain. The team management has added uncapped wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra as a replacement in the squad. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may finally get an opportunity to play after being on the sidelines for nine matches. Batting coach Sitanshu Kotak emphasized the need for patience regarding Sooryavanshi's exposure to international cricket.

title: Shreyas Iyer on verge of breaking Rohit Sharma's unique T20I captaincy record
content: Iyer, who took over as India's T20I captain from Suryakumar Yadav in June, has scored 632 runs in 22 matches as skipper this year.

title: Trump eases tariffs on Canadian imports weeks before US midterms
content: The White House said the changes would remove tariffs on certain products, including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment". However, the administration will also introduce tariffs on other goods, including carpets, certain valves and waste products. The new measures will take effect on October 30. The United States and Canada have closely connected economies.

title: Cabinet secretariat merely acknowledged complaint of Election Commissioners': RTI
content: Explaining the rationale behind the reluctance to take any action, a confidential note on the file shared by the Cabinet secretariat with transparency activist, Commodore Lokesh K Batra (Retd), as part of its 21-page RTI reply, stated that EC being a Constitutional body is insulated from the Executive's interference by design.

title: Centre bans reuse of single-use medical devices across hospitals
content: In a letter dated Oct 16, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said it had come to its notice that some private and corporate hospitals were reusing single-use devices after sterilising them, including items used in cardiology, nephrology, oncology, cardiothoracic and vascular surgery (CTVS), neurosurgery and other clinical services. The DGHS said that reuse could expose patients to cross-infection, device malfunction, reduced performance and other complications.

title: Two critical PHP flaws trigger global alert; millions of services face cyber risk
content: PHP advised users on Oct 23 to temporarily disable its session upload progress feature until the next regular bugfix release. The warning followed an earlier advisory on Oct 21 about a related vulnerability. The latest issue affects applications only when specific session settings are changed while running and the upload progress feature remains enabled. Users who have already disabled the feature do not need to take further action.

title: Cuba next? Trump hints at 'little stopover' after US warships return from Iran war
content: Trump and Rubio have both adopted a hard line towards Cuba's communist government. In May, the two renewed the possibility of US military intervention, with the threat gaining further significance after the Trump administration announced criminal charges against former Cuban leader Raúl Castro. Trump had floated a similar idea earlier this year but had not raised it publicly in recent months.

title: ‘A racist terror attack’: Emmanuel Macron condemns deadly shooting near Paris
content: "These people were targeted because of their skin colour or perceived religion, and for no other reason," Macron said after meeting officials and residents in Trappes. "There is no place for this in France." Macron also said the suspect's statements indicated that the attack had been planned in advance. Police arrested the suspect less than 20 minutes after the shooting began.

title: Need to unite against divisive forces, tackle new challenges: PM Modi
content: Inaugurating the Chinmaya Amrit Mahotsav Global Sammelan, he said Swami Chinmayananda set his goals as per issues facing the country at the time and new challenges had emerged in the past few decades. “We must unite society against divisive forces. We must inspire citizens toward self-reliance, and we must connect every individual to vision of a developed India by 2047. For these objectives, we must become more proactive,” he said.

title: Ukrainian soldier cuts off his own foot to survive, rescued by drone after 8 months
content: Kostiantyn Vlasenko, 49, had been stranded in a boiler room with severe injuries after a Russian drone strike. With no way to escape and little hope of being rescued, he made a desperate decision to amputate his remaining foot to survive. On October 4, a large drone lifted him into the air using a harness and carried him 15km to safety.

title: Opposition's 'mock Parliament' to step up fight against SIR & CEC Gyanesh Kumar
content: Sources said a “mock” gathering depicting an assembly of MPs may take place in the national capital on Oct 28. The event will involve MPs and others, but is unlikely to be a large gathering, given that a massive show of strength to push for the CEC’s resignation is planned at Ramlila Maidan as a “Delhi chalo” rally.

title: Arms training case: US mercenary VanDyke, 6 Ukrainians to remain abroad till Feb 24
content: VanDyke attended the court hearing Friday and sought the release of his seized personal articles. The seven accused had earlier sought six weeks to meet their families and were allowed to stay abroad till Oct 23. They were arrested on March 13 for allegedly training the insurgent-linked groups in Myanmar.

title: Northwest India turned drier, south wetter over 70 years, finds IMD study
content: In northwest India, the hot semi-arid zone grew from about a quarter of the region’s area in 1951-1980 to a third in 1991-2020, while the temperate zone shrank from about a quarter to less than a fifth, meaning that an area equal to roughly 7% of the region moved into the drier zone as temperatures rose and rainfall declined, said the study.

title: Brics parliamentary meet should end with joint statement: LS Speaker Om Birla
content: Talking to reporters Friday, Birla said the forum in India would work towards consensus-based dialogue on the role of Parliament in strengthening institutions, promotion of human-centred innovation in AI and digital technologies through Parliament, more representative system of global governance and role of Parliament in ensuring a sustainable and inclusive future for Brics countries.

title: New norms for cars from 2029: Rear-crash tests, data recorders
content: The ministry has set mandatory timelines for automakers to comply with other Automotive Industry Standards (AIS), covering occupant protection in offset frontal and lateral collisions, protection of pedestrians and other vulnerable road users, and fitment of immobilisers. The requirements will come into effect from April 2027 onwards. In a notification, the ministry also made AIS-192 mandatory for Event Data Recorders (EDRs) installed in cars from Oct 2029.

title: After Op Sindoor friction, Delhi & Baku reset ties with EAM Jaishankar's visit
content: Ties between the two countries had been held back by geopolitical reasons for a while, mainly Azerbaijan’s ties with Pakistan — as evident from its support for Islamabad after Op Sindoor last year — and India’s defence ties with Armenia. While Bayramov spoke about taking the relationship to a higher level, setting aside past differences, Jaishankar underlined the significance of trade and energy cooperation. Terrorism was also discussed.

title: Study traces how an El Niño changed the pollution map
content: Coming ahead of India’s peak pollution season, the paper, titled ‘Air quality in flux: The baffling ENSO transition in India’, published in Atmospheric Pollution Research journal Thursday, found that La Niña/El Niño conditions altered atmospheric circulation, PM2.5 transport pathways and weather conditions that determine whether pollution disperses or gets trapped.

title: On Congress' 175-200 Seats Demand In UP, Samajwadi's 'Winnability' Reply
content: Not many within the Samajwadi Party are convinced of the Congress' political heft to demand 175-200 seats, the 2024 Lok Sabha poll results notwithstanding, sources said.

title: Trump Warns Of "Another Little Epic Fury", Iran's "Don't Play With Fire" Reply
content: Trump did not outline the conditions Iran would have to meet to prevent another round of military action.

title: First Tanker Carrying Russian Diesel Sets Sail For US Under Trump-Putin Deal
content: Marine intelligence firm Kpler said the vessel signaled that it was headed to New York to arrive November 7 and would be the first Russian diesel delivery to the United States since July 2023.

title: Video Captures Gunmen Opening Fire At Jordan Church Funeral, Killing 7
content: A government statement said that the attack was "carried out by unknown assailants," but didn't say whether any gunmen were captured or killed. It said that "investigations are underway at full speed."

title: Kerala Governor's Veg-Only Order For Lok Bhavan Kitchen On Day 1 Sparks Row
content: KC Venugopal remined the Governor that his constitutional position required him to protect rights guaranteed by the Constitution, including the freedom to eat food of one's choice.

title: Bodies Of 3 Keralites Who Died In German Apartment Fire Brought Home
content: Officials at Cochin International Airport Limited (CIAL) said the bodies of Johny and Joy arrived at the airport early Friday.

title: Bhagwant Mann Slams Centre On Being 'Detained' At Delhi Airport, BJP Replies
content: Bhagwant Mann alleged that he was made to sit for two hours and claimed that the head of the Customs Department at the Delhi airport was the brother of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.

title: "Don't Play With Fire": Iran Warns Of Undersea Cable Attacks If War Resumes
content: The official warned Washington not to "play with fire", and said Iran had full access to the undersea cables and could easily destroy them.

title: "Situation Dire": Melania Trump Secures Ceasefire In Ukrainian City
content: The localised ceasefire in Russian-occupied Oleshky would begin on October 29, a statement issued by her office said. There was no immediate confirmation from Moscow or Kyiv.

title: Delhi Plans Rs 99 Crore Wall Along Yamuna To Prevent Flooding
content: The reinforced cement concrete (RCC) wall will be built between the Magazine Road drain and the Old Railway Bridge, one of the most closely monitored points on the Yamuna during the monsoon.

title: Kim Jong Un Calls For "Military Revolution" As He Urges Stronger Army Units
content: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un called for the country's army companies to be turned into elite, self-sufficient combat units during a two-day meeting of company commanders in Pyongyang, state media KCNA said on Saturday.

title: Trump Lifts Some Canada Tariffs Ahead Of Midterm Elections
content: The easing of tariffs will apply to products including "plywood sheets, some paper products, certain machinery and refrigeration equipment," the White House said in a statement.

title: CBI Arrests Two ED Officials In Rs 5 Lakh Bribery Case
content: The CBI laid a trap and allegedly caught Manoj Dwivedi red-handed while demanding and accepting Rs 5 lakh on behalf of the Enforcement Officer for extending favour to the complainant's father in the case.

title: Ukraine Says It Will Observe Ceasefire In Russian-Occupied Oleshky
content: The statement from Ukraine military command said: "To carry out a humanitarian operation in the temporarily occupied town of Oleshky in the Kherson region, Ukraine is implementing a ceasefire in a designated area starting at 3:00 am on October 27, Kyiv time.

title: Gunman Kills 1, Injures 4 In Town Outside Paris: Police
content: The shooting comes as France is on edge following riots on the sidelines of mass protests over the cost of living last weekend, which saw some of the worst street violence the country has seen in recent years.
